name: River Serpent
author: James Wyatt with Ashlie Hope
pdfPageNumbering: One-based page number, counting the cover.
section: An Amonkhet Bestiary, The Luxa River
appearanceEvidence: The river text describes the more mundane serpent as resembling a Giant Constrictor Snake. The blue scaling and crest are editorial choices based on the general River Serpent illustration. The artwork depicts a more dramatic specimen with flipperlike limbs, which are omitted for this constrictor depiction.
habitatEvidence: The river section places serpent encounters toward the river bottom in the Luxa. Amonkhet, Luxa River and Riverbed are searchable tags derived from the prose.
printedIllustration: Christopher Moeller, River Serpent, on p. 38.

reskinReference.name: Giant Constrictor Snake
reskinReference.officialRulesWitness: Wizards of the Coast System Reference Document 5.1, p. 374
reskinReference.scope: CR 2 ordinary River Serpent. The behir-based variation belongs to the separate Giant River Serpent entry.

name: Serpopard
author: James Wyatt with Ashlie Hope
pdfPageNumbering: One-based page number, counting the cover.
appearanceEvidence: Creature description and Tyler Jacobson’s Prowling Serpopard illustration on p. 37.
habitatEvidence: The prose explicitly places it in trees near desert oases and along the Luxa River inside the Hekma. The tags restate those locations.
printedIllustration: Tyler Jacobson, Prowling Serpopard, on p. 37.
sourceIssue: Pounce requires a Claw hit. Bite is the only printed action. Do not add an inferred Claw attack or change the trigger to Bite.

name: Kavu Predator
author: James Wyatt with Ashlie Hope
pdfPageNumbering: One-based page number, counting the cover.
section: Elves of Llanowar, Kavu, Arboreal Foes
appearanceEvidence: Kavu are reptilian, and the arboreal section describes climbing breeds. Broad claws and angular features draw on the adjacent Kavu Climber illustration. Color is editorial.
habitatEvidence: The Kelfae breed arboreal kavu in Llanowar. Forest canopy and Kelfae woodlands are editorial tags derived from the Elves of Llanowar section and Kavu text.
printedIllustration: Jonathan Kuo, Kavu Climber, on p. 24.

name: Steel Leaf Kavu
author: James Wyatt with Ashlie Hope
pdfPageNumbering: One-based page number, counting the cover.
section: Elves of Llanowar, Kavu, Deadly Chargers
appearanceEvidence: The section describes riding breeds. The pose-independent features draw on the visible mount anatomy in Chris Rahn’s Steel Leaf Champion illustration.
habitatEvidence: The source describes the Basiphem maintaining forest-floor stables for their largest ground-dwelling kavu. The habitat tags condense that location and the Llanowar setting.
printedIllustration: Chris Rahn, Steel Leaf Champion, beside the stat block on p. 24. This printed art citation is documentation only.
